items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: No iterate-spec file at small complexity; matches the operator's explicit task verbatim — anchor or disclose-and-accept each of the four _GENERATED_PREFIXES entries in is_safe_to_skip_review, starting with the confirmed-consumer prefix (.shipwright/compliance/ci-security.json read by security_gate.py). All four addressed: two anchored (iterates/, CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/), two removed with disclosed reasoning (compliance/, runtime/).

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: Pure path-classification functions, no I/O, no external calls; string/regex operations only, all total functions (no exceptions to catch).

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: This IS the security-sensitive file (PR-review skip-gate classifier). No raw input reaches SQL/HTML. No secrets. The change closes a real gap (ci-security.json trusted as a deploy-gate oracle with no provenance check) rather than introducing one.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: Each new anchor has a positive (still skip-safe) and negative (attacker-chosen shape, no longer skip-safe) test; asserts on classifier outcomes (is_safe_to_skip_review / is_generated_path return values), never internals. Updated two now-inaccurate fixtures in test_review_record_tier.py that used since-removed compliance-prefix skip-safety.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: O(1) string prefix/partition checks and a couple of small compiled-regex matches per path; no loops over unbounded data, no N+1 pattern (this runs once per changed path in a PR).

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: pr_review_generated.py is now 386 lines, over the 300-line guideline (was 276 before this diff). Disclosed rather than split in this run: the file's own established convention is dense, chronologically-ordered rationale comments per anchoring round (Round 1-5 already present before this diff), and splitting the classification logic from its round-by-round rationale would separate code from the reasoning a future round needs to extend it safely. Flagging for the code-reviewer to weigh in; will split if it agrees a split is warranted without losing that traceability.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: Producer/consumer pairs verified by reading the write-time source directly (not guessed): .shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/ entries are written by iterate_entry.entry_file_for + iterate_test_results.install_immutable_evidence, both already enforcing RUN_ID_STRICT — verified via RUN_ID_STRICT.fullmatch at read time here too. CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/ drops are written by write_changelog_drop._next_counter_path (category + '_NNN.md'), matched by the new _is_canonical_changelog_drop. No new serialized format introduced, so no new round-trip probe script; the check performed was tracing the real producer code plus the new negative-case tests below.
